req_desc:
Sign-in and landing routes.
Each role signs in and lands on its published route, as detailed in Public screens and controls.

Landing routes survive reload.
Reloading or directly opening any published route shows the same screen for a signed-in user with access to it.

Verifier firm boundary.
A verifier can read and act only on windows assigned to their own firm, and any other window answers exactly as an unknown one does.

Role refusals at the server.
Every role-restricted action is refused by the server for any other role, whatever the browser shows.

Server-decided window opening.
A window opens for meter intake only when the server's clock has passed its published opening instant.

Exact meter conversion.
Meter readings in every published unit and interval convert to integer watt-hours exactly, and a line that is not a whole watt-hour refuses the whole pull with that line named.

Meter hub outage.
When the meter hub is unreachable, a pull changes nothing and shows the published banner.

Automatic gap repair.
Gaps of two hours or less fill by straight line and longer gaps by the same local clock hour one week earlier, as qualified in Business rules.

Estimates never seed estimates.
An Estimated hour is never the source of another estimate, and an hour with no permitted source stays Missing.

Typed substitutions.
The analyst replaces a Missing or Estimated hour with a typed whole watt-hour value and a reason, and the hour reads Substituted.

Hour Wall grid.
The Hour Wall is one keyboard-walkable grid holding exactly one cell per window hour, each cell stating its date, hour, consumed, matched and quality in words.

Hour panel survives live refresh.
An open hour panel and its typed value stay intact while the window refreshes behind it, and a live refresh keeps focus on the same wall hour.

Gap repair journey.
An analyst takes a window from ten Missing hours to none using only the desk, and the scores update in place.

Merit order by every input.
Lots reorder by keyboard, touch and pointer, change position only on the server's reply, persist, and each new rank is announced.

Competing reorders.
When two analysts change one window from the same revision, exactly one wins and the other gets the published refusal naming who wrote and when.

Closed lot drawer is gone.
A closed lot drawer, like every other closed overlay and collapsed panel, is hidden and takes no focus or tap at every viewport width.

Lot exclusion in place.
Excluding or including a lot updates the wall, the four scores and the unmatched total without a reload and announces the result.

Same-hour same-zone matching.
A certificate matches only consumption in its own production hour at a site in its own bidding zone, and hourly surplus stays in holdings.

Battery-shifted lots.
Battery-shifted lots match on the discharge hour at the published round-trip factor, with the remainder posted to a named loss line.

Exact bundle splits.
Every bundle splits only on its watt-hour range, and its pieces are contiguous and sum exactly to the original.

Repeatable allocation.
Allocation is greedy by lot rank, runs on the server, and produces the same lines and digest for the same inputs.

Paired watt-hour ledger.
Every movement is one equal pair of entries, corrections are reversals, and the published balances always equal the registry's opening total.

Residual emissions on unmatched hours.
Unmatched hours carry whole grams of residual emissions from decimal grid factors, rounded per hour as qualified in Services.

Holdings sync.
A holdings sync imports registry bundles the desk does not yet hold, gives each same-zone bundle to the first window that synced it, and posts each import to the ledger.

Announced allocation results.
Each allocation result is announced once with the new hourly score and unmatched-hour count on the server's reply, and another person's change is announced once per revision.

Four grain scores.
The server publishes month, week, day and hour scores in integer basis points computed at read time, and they never rise toward hour.

Break the Month control.
A four-detent slider moves between MONTH, WEEK, DAY and HOUR by drag, tap and keyboard, holds its grain in the address, and opens hours from its wall.

Break the Month sequence.
Each detent move runs split, then fall, then count, reverses on the way back, and an interrupted move ends on the latest detent's server value with only that detent announced.

Reduced motion and thumb use.
With reduced motion, including a change made while the page is open, or by thumb at phone width, Break the Month gives the same four server scores, the same cells and the same announcement.

Submission gate.
A window enters review only when it has no Missing hour, has an assigned firm and is Reconciling.

Deterministic sample.
The 25 sampled hours are drawn by the published hash, and nobody can choose or swap them.

Recording the sample.
A verifier records agreement or an exception on every sampled hour and completes the review.

Server-fixed opinion.
The server fixes the opinion as Qualified above the published non-Actual share or with any exception, and nobody can set it.

Review layouts at published widths.
The review screen changes layout exactly at the two published widths and at no other, and its evidence collapses on the phone as qualified in Interactions.

Returned windows.
A verifier returns a window with a reason, the analyst resumes it, and every other action is refused while it is Returned.

Review time limit.
From the exact deadline instant every read reports the window Returned with the published line and every verifier write is refused, whatever the device clock shows.

Server-decided lot expiry.
A lot past its cancel-by instant reads Expired from the server's clock and leaves allocation on the next computation.

One cancellation per line.
One allocation line produces one accepted registry cancellation, however many times the button is pressed, and a successor window never re-sends a copied Confirmed line.

Cancelled only on confirmation.
A lot reads Cancelled only after the registry confirms every one of its lines, never on submission, and the confirmed-lines count always equals the recorded confirmations.

Rejected lines.
A rejected line becomes unmatched, recomputes the scores and sends the window back to Reconciling, as qualified in Business rules.

Registry outage.
When the registry is unreachable, submission changes no line it could not send and shows the published banner.

Signing by the verifier.
Only the assigned verifier signs a Cancelled window, by typing their own name, and the signature is kept even when the press is down.

Three-part seal.
A window reads Sealed only with its signature recorded, its PDF rendered and the store's returned bytes matching the recorded digest.

Held seal recovery.
A seal held by a press or store outage finishes by itself once the service returns, with no restart.

Attestation PDF contents.
The issued PDF carries the published statement lines for its window with names exactly as written, and never carries working notes.

Seal journey.
A verifier signs a window and, after sealing, lands on the new statement's public route.

Public check page.
The public check verifies the signature over the bytes the store returns on every request, states the result, and exposes no working notes.

Restatement.
A late meter correction to a Sealed window makes it Restated and opens a successor, while the old statement and its exact PDF bytes stay checkable.

Statement reader journey.
A reader with no account finds a statement by code, reads the result and downloads the PDF.

Site-zone day and week cuts.
Day and week buckets cut at the site's own midnight with Monday week starts, while hours stay keyed in UTC.

Matching policy and verifier assignment.
The lead sets each site's matching target and assigns a verifier firm to a window within the published state limits, and a signed window keeps its frozen target.

Group score table.
The lead reads every window's four scores and its on-target word on one screen.

Server time on every screen.
Every time-based screen state comes from the server, so a wrong device clock changes nothing.

Dialog keyboard contract.
Every dialog takes focus, keeps Tab inside itself, closes on Escape recording nothing, shows its refusals inside itself, and returns focus to its opener, as qualified in Interactions for a successful spread.

Responsive layouts.
Every screen follows the published layout matrix, switching exactly at 768 and 1200 pixels, with no sideways page scrolling down to 320 pixels.

Motion restraint.
Motion follows the published timing attributes, nothing unnamed loops, and reduced motion, applied at once when it changes, removes all movement while keeping every function.

Server boundary and boot.
The server serves only the published surface, enforces the published size limit and starts when any dependency except its own database is down.

Hero poster.
The public home page is the published full-bleed poster with the cropped meter and headline.

Poster language on working screens.
Every working screen carries the published flat colour fields, large figures and blunt copy.

Credentials and real integrations.
Service credentials come only from the environment, and every provider result shown is one the server really received.

Lifetime ranges stay exact.
Registry ranges above the largest whole number a browser number holds exactly travel as digit strings, show exactly with thousands commas, and reach the registry as the same exact integers.

Exact text and field errors.
Reasons and notes are stored and shown exactly as written, limits count Unicode code points, and each refused field shows its published message, as qualified in Business rules.

Server-derived countdowns.
Every countdown runs from the server's remaining seconds by elapsed time, asks again once at zero and shows what the server answers.

Session ends mid-task.
When a session ends during work, a sign-in dialog opens over the current screen, typed work stays, and the refused write is resent once after sign-in.

Board filter in the address.
The window board filters in place from a sheet, keeps the filter in the address through reload and back, and the closed sheet is hidden and inert.

Resizing keeps work.
Crossing either published width keeps open panels, typed values, wall selection and focus, as qualified in Interactions.

Break the Month to scale.
Every block and hour cell publishes its server watt-hours and is drawn to scale, and each falling piece publishes the server's detached watt-hours for its parent bucket.

Group site tree.
The lead walks sites and their windows in one tree with a single tab stop, closed children are absent, and choosing a site filters the table in place.

Hour Wall range selection.
Shift+Arrow, Shift+click and a touch mode select the UTC-ordered run of hours between anchor and focus, and the selection survives live refreshes.

Spread a total.
A typed total spread across 2 to 168 consecutive Missing or Estimated hours follows the published weights and remainder rule and always sums exactly to the total.

Stale panel recovery.
A stale hour panel offers a retry on the latest revision with the typed body unchanged, and its read-only figures follow live refreshes while its typed fields never change.

Remote changes keep focus.
Another analyst's reorder or exclusion keeps focus on the same lot's equivalent control, with no extra announcement.

Versioned corrections.
The highest version per hour wins whatever the arrival order, a later meter pull never overwrites a corrected hour, and any refused pull applies nothing.

Restatement chain.
One pull opens exactly one successor for a restated window, every successor keeps the base window id and takes the next statement code, and each statement points only to its immediate successor.

Second-pass cancellation.
A kept Pending line rejected during a later pass follows the published transitions, and the next pass sends only lines never accepted.

Review deadline capped by cancel-by.
The review deadline is the earlier of the review period's end and the earliest cancel-by among lots holding an Unsubmitted line.

Settlement time on every desk screen.
Every desk screen shows the settlement time, running from the latest server time by elapsed time.

Row timers share one re-ask.
The board and the queue show a countdown on each In review row, and rows reaching zero together share one re-ask.

Review by keyboard.
A verifier records all 25 sampled hours from the keyboard with the published keys, one request per result and focus moving on the server's reply.

Where it went.
Each bucket below HOUR opens a list of its worst finer buckets from the server, hidden and inert when closed at every width.

Grain replies carry revision.
A grain reply older than the highest revision seen is discarded and asked again once, a failed grain returns the slider to its last settled detent, and a live change while settled updates the numeral in place.

Hour panel in browser history.
An hour panel is one browser history entry, so Back closes it recording nothing and returns focus to that hour's cell, and Forward reopens it with empty fields.

Dialogs survive the deadline.
An open dialog and its typed text survive a deadline passing behind it, and its save then renders the server's refusal inside the dialog.

Signing across a session end.
A signature refused by an ended session is resent once after sign-in and produces one signature, and a held seal finishing during sign-in still lands on its statement.

Signing-key replacement.
A firm's verifier replaces its signing key, every signature records the key in force at signing, and the public check uses only that recorded key.

Sync every touched month.
A holdings sync asks for every UTC month its window's hours touch, ascending, and imports each bundle id once.

Battery timing checks.
A battery bundle with an unusable discharge hour is deposited and never allocates or posts loss, and one discharging outside the window stays in holdings with no line or loss.

Exact MWh on the statement.
Statements and the signed payload carry consumed and hour-matched watt-hours, and the PDF prints them in MWh with exactly six decimals built from integer digits.

Meter pull result.
A finished meter pull announces how many hours were read and how many are still Missing before the allocation line.

Group totals.
Each month's group totals are summed matched over summed consumed at each grain, never an average of window scores, counting a successor in place of its Restated predecessor.

Lot confirmation counts.
Each lot publishes its confirmed and total line counts, computed at read and shown in place with no reload.

Reassignment ends access.
Reassigning a window to another firm ends the former firm's access at its next read and on any open page, and clears the sample and its results even when the digest is unchanged.

Provider error text stays out.
Raw provider error text never reaches an API body or a screen, and only published copy does.

Hour detail unclipped.
Hour detail opened from the far right of the sideways-scrolled wall at phone width is wholly in view, unclipped and above the sticky headers.

One outcome at the deadline.
A review completed as its deadline arrives gets one outcome, and simultaneous reads at the deadline raise the window's revision exactly once.

Already-received lines stay Pending.
A registry answer that a line was already received keeps that line Pending under the same line id, and every other 4xx rejects it.

Signing fixes everything but the name.
Any opinion, signing time or statement code sent with the typed name changes nothing the server fixes.

Group totals stay with the lead.
A verifier is refused the group totals, and every list a verifier can read counts only their own firm's windows.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and _schema run-manifest-v1.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package with its licence, plus the Unbounded and Onest typefaces with their licence; shipped packages means the production dependency tree, that is, the non-dev group of the Python lockfile or requirements.
Every shipped package and typeface is under MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, PSF or the SIL Open Font License.
The app uses no datastore beyond the PostgreSQL and MinIO services named in this brief.
The provided service configuration and the published WireMock baseline stay untouched.
Python dependencies are installed into .venv inside /app, and no manifest command relies on a globally installed package.
